original_question: Let X be a compact subset of R^n with positive Lebesgue measure, where n > 2, and let ms_r(X) denote the largest measure that is guaranteed for a monochromatic symmetric subset in every measurable r-coloring of X. Classify the numbers ms_r(X) for such sets X. In particular, determine ms_r(X) for every regular convex polyhedron in R^n with n > 2, and determine ms_2(T) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.4: classify the maximal symmetry numbers ms_r(X) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n for n>2; in particular, compute ms_r(X) for regular convex polyhedra in R^n, n>2, and compute ms_2(T) (equivalently ms_2(S_4 × I)) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the higher-dimensional classification problem for maximal symmetry numbers of compact positive-measure subsets of R^n, and it preserves the two explicit special cases singled out in the paper: regular convex polyhedra and the regular tetrahedron in R^3. It also correctly frames ms_r(X) in terms of measurable r-colorings and guaranteed monochromatic symmetric subsets.
missing_details: The admissible symmetry family must be stated explicitly: in the relevant geometric setup, X is endowed with S = Iso(X) \ {id}, the family of all nonidentity isometries of X.
A 'symmetric subset' should be defined in the paper’s formal sense: a measurable subset B ⊂ X such that B = s(B) for some admissible symmetry s ∈ S.

The paper’s formal definition of ms_r(X) should be given, not only the informal guarantee interpretation: ms_r(X) is defined via an infimum over measurable r-colorings and a supremum over monochromatic symmetric measurable subsets.

The measure on X should be specified explicitly through the symmetry-measure-space formalism; the paper suppresses this in the problem statement, so a stand-alone version should say what measure on X is being used.
The color parameter should be quantified as a finite integer r ≥ 2 in this geometric problem, even though Section 3 defines ms_r for general cardinals.
The problem is posed as the higher-dimensional extension of the already classified plane case in Theorem 5.3; mentioning that connection makes the scope sharper and more paper-faithful.
The tetrahedron clause should retain the paper’s explicit equivalent reformulation: 'calculate ms_2(T) (or equivalently, ms_2(S_4 × I))', with I = [0,1].
refined_question: Extend the plane classification of Theorem 5.3 to higher dimensions: for each integer r ≥ 2, let X ⊂ R^n be a compact set of positive Lebesgue measure, regarded as a symmetry measure space with admissible symmetries S = Iso(X) \ {id}, and define ms_r(X) to be the maximal symmetry number of X, i.e. the infimum, over all measurable r-colorings χ : X → {1, ..., r}, of the supremum of μ(B) over all measurable monochromatic subsets B ⊂ X for which B = s(B) for some s ∈ S. Classify ms_r(X) for all n > 2. In particular, determine ms_r(X) for every regular convex polyhedron X in R^n with n > 2, and determine ms_2(T) for the regular tetrahedron T ⊂ R^3.
equivalent_formulation: Determine ms_2(S_4 × I), where I = [0,1]; the paper states this as equivalent to determining ms_2(T) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3.
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 5.4 in Section 5, introduced immediately after Theorem 5.3. Your draft matches that problem closely, but it leaves implicit the section-3 formal definition of maximal symmetry numbers and the section-5 choice of admissible symmetries. The refined version restores those hidden assumptions, keeps the exact higher-dimensional scope n>2, preserves the paper’s two highlighted special cases, and retains the tetrahedron/S_4 × I equivalence exactly as stated in the paper. The nearby context also shows that this problem is meant as the higher-dimensional continuation of the complete n=2 classification in Theorem 5.3, with Proposition 5.5 supplying the adjacent asymptotic bounds for regular convex polyhedra.
